paper.title: On Tiny Episodic Memories in Continual Learning
paper.read_range: PDF pages 1–4: title/abstract, §§1–4, Algorithm 1; no claim to have read or reproduced remaining benchmark results.
paper.inspection: §4 differentiates direct example replay from gradient projection; Alg.1 lines 5–7 samples current B_n and memory B_M and applies SGD(B_n union B_M, theta, lr). Both gradients are computed at current theta.
paper.short_quote: Single gradient step to update the parameters by stacking current minibatch with minibatch from memory
paper.scope: Supervised continual-learning ER definition; its one-pass protocol and tiny episodic memory differ from this lesson's finite-dataset repeated SFT. No transfer of the paper's reported gains to TinyLM.

official_code.pin_method: git ls-remote https://github.com/facebookresearch/agem.git HEAD; GitHub tree response matched this SHA.

files.inspection: Memory examples/labels concatenate with current examples/labels, then sess.run(model.train, model.reg_loss) uses that batch; reservoir stores examples, not old gradients.
FC ER loss is mean cross entropy; optimizer computes gradients of current reg_loss with respect to shared trainable variables; apply_gradients performs the update.

official_code.scope: Primary authors' implementation, inspected only. No TensorFlow benchmark or third-party training run.

pytorch.read_lines: 1200–1239, CrossEntropyLoss class-index formula and mean/sum reductions
pytorch.inspection: Class-index loss masks ignore_index. Unweighted mean divides the sum over nonignored positions by their count; this course explicitly uses reduction=sum and divides by its own valid-target count. Inputs/PAD and example counts therefore need not equal supervision weights.
pytorch.scope: Installed official source is the actually inspected original; remote blob contents were not additionally downloaded.
